memoryText: And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and said, The LORD, he is God; the LORD, he is God.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 1 Kings 18:39 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is the people’s response on Mount Carmel after fire falls from heaven. It is a simple confession, repeated for emphasis, and it is the heart of what the prophets were sent to say.

“When all the people saw it.” They had been standing on the fence. Elijah asked them how long they would go limping between two opinions, and they had said nothing. Now they see. God does not always answer prayer with fire from heaven, but when he acts, his people recognize it.

“They fell on their faces.” This is the posture of worship and of surrender. It is not a casual nod of agreement. They are overwhelmed. They realize that they have been wrong.

“The LORD, he is God.” This is the confession that Israel was made for. The Hebrew is emphatic: Yahweh, he is the God. It echoes the Shema: “The LORD our God, the LORD is one.” And it echoes Elijah’s own name, “My God is Yahweh.” All of Elijah’s mission is encapsulated in this sentence.

“The LORD, he is God.” The repetition is the people’s way of saying it with their whole heart. They say it twice because they cannot say it enough.

In the days of the divided kingdom, the question was always, “Who is God?” Baal or the LORD? Money or the LORD? The king or the LORD? The same question faces us. This verse is an invitation to make the confession again. Not just once, but daily. The LORD, he is God. Christ is Lord (Philippians 2:11). Say it when you are tempted to serve something else.
weekInReview: This week you followed the divided kingdom into the age of Elijah and Elisha. You read Psalms 42 and 43, the cry of a soul thirsting for God, with the refrain “Hope in God.” You saw Elijah announce the drought, be fed by ravens, and confront the prophets of Baal on Carmel, where fire fell and the people confessed, “The LORD, he is God.” You saw the same prophet, exhausted and afraid, meet God in a low whisper at Horeb. You read the story of Naboth’s vineyard, and the lone prophet Micaiah. You watched Elijah taken to heaven and Elisha take up the mantle, and you read the miracles of Elisha for widows, a Shunammite, and the hungry. The week taught that God is the one true God, that he cares for the weak, and that he speaks even in whispers.
reflectionQuestions: Elijah moved from triumph on Carmel to despair under the broom tree. How does God’s gentle care of him encourage you in a season of exhaustion?
Elisha’s miracles of provision and resurrection point to Jesus, the bread of life and the conqueror of death. Which of these miracles speaks most to a need you have right now?
Naboth was wronged by the powerful, and God sent a prophet to defend him. Who in your world needs someone to speak up for them?
prayerPrompts: Tell God that the LORD, he is God, and why you say it.
Thank him for answering by fire and speaking in a whisper.
Thank him for caring for the poor and grieving.
